entries.title: NASA Selects Blue Origin as Mars Telecommunications Network Provider
entries.content:
[![NASA insignia.](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/nasa_meatball_large.jpg?w=2048)](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/nasa_meatball_large.jpg)

Credit: NASA

NASA awarded Blue Origin a contract Tuesday to develop the agency’s Mars Telecommunications Network, a next-generation communications system that will enable reliable, high-bandwidth communications and navigation services for current and future Mars missions.

The firm-fixed-price contract has a maximum potential value of approximately $700 million to deliver a high-performance Mars telecommunications orbiter to NASA no later than Dec. 31, 2028.

Blue Origin will design, develop, integrate, launch, and operate the network as a part of the agency’s broader space communications and navigation infrastructure. The architecture will consist of a high-performance telecommunications spacecraft orbiting Mars, transmitting science data, imagery, navigation information, and critical mission communications for spacecraft operating on and around the planet.

The award marks a milestone in NASA’s strategy to expand communications and navigation services beyond Earth and the Moon, establishing the foundation for sustained exploration of Mars in the coming decades.

Under the Artemis program, NASA is sending astronauts to explore the Moon and prepare for missions to Mars. Robotic missions will pave the way for human exploration of the Red Planet, and as these missions expand, demand for data will continue to increase. To meet this need, NASA is pursuing a purpose-built network capable of supporting a growing number of missions while providing greater capacity, reliability, and operational flexibility.

The selection follows NASA’s request for proposal [issued](https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/61134227fd0b4729813a5b863ee4bef4/view) in May. As the agency increasingly taps commercial partners for transportation and communications services in Earth orbit and to develop the Moon Base, the Mars Telecommunications Network initiative similarly seeks to harness private-sector capabilities while enabling NASA to focus on exploration and scientific discovery.

The network, managed by NASA’s Space Communications and Navigation program, is expected to be operational at Mars by 2030 and will support both current and future missions to the Red Planet, as NASA ventures deeper into space.

For more information about NASA’s space communications efforts, visit:

[**https://www.nasa.gov/communicating-with-missions**](https://www.nasa.gov/communicating-with-missions)

-end-

entries.title: A sustainable flame retardant derived from corn steep liquor
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Certain phosphorus compounds are highly effective at suppressing fires, which is why they are widely used in flame retardants. Phosphorus, however, is a finite resource. Estimates suggest it could be depleted within the next 50–300 years. That is why, as part of the ScaleAmP project, a research team is working to extract phosphorus from corn steep liquor, a byproduct of starch production.

entries.title: AI-informed AdaptiveFlow redefines large-scale cloud computing for drug discovery
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Researchers today announced AdaptiveFlow, an AI-informed platform that can virtually screen billions of drug-like molecules with a 1,000-fold reduction in computational costs over existing methods. Developed and validated by scientists from St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, University of Pavia, Dana Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School, AdaptiveFlow allows prohibitively expensive ultra-large virtual drug screens to be conducted routinely. The open-source platform was published today in Nature Biotechnology.

entries.title: What Google Cloud announced in AI this month
entries.content:
***Editor’s note****: Want to keep up with the latest from Google Cloud? Check back here for a monthly recap of our latest updates, announcements, resources, events, learning opportunities, and more.*

---

This month, we focused on making AI highly practical for your business, including its associated costs. This meant tailoring our models for specialized industries – starting with Financial Services and Legal –  and helping you keep your budgets under control. Let’s dive in! 

### **Top announcements**

* [FinOps for the AI era: New flexible billing and cost controls for agents:](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/flexible-billing-and-cost-controls-for-agents-on-google-cloud?e=48754805) To help you get better return on AI, we announced expanded billing flexibility and new cost management tools for agent workloads across Gemini Enterprise and developer tools like Google Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise and Android Studio.
* [Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/introducing-gemini-enterprise-for-financial-services?e=48754805): We’re bringing Google’s agentic AI directly into the workflows of capital markets and corporate banking.
* [Gemini Enterprise for Legal](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/introducing-gemini-enterprise-for-legal?e=48754805): Gemini Enterprise for Legal provides an integrated, fully governed environment configured for rapid deployment across firms and corporate legal departments.
* [Expanding Google Antigravity for enterprise customers:](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/expanding-google-antigravity-for-enterprise-customers?e=48754805) Antigravity is available now as part of eligible Gemini Enterprise app subscriptions, including out-of-the-box administrative and spend controls.

### **Thought leadership (editor’s pick):**

* [Tokenomics: Why smart teams spend more on AI, on purpose](https://cloud.google.com/transform/tokenomics-why-smart-teams-spend-more-on-ai-on-purpose?e=48754805): Hear from Eric Lam, Head of Value, Delta, Google Cloud Consulting about how disciplined organizations are moving past reactive sticker shock over AI bills and embracing tokenomics.
* [Meet the researcher fighting AI hallucinations at Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/transform/meet-the-researcher-fighting-ai-hallucinations-at-google-cloud?e=48754805): Cyrus is a senior research scientist at Google. Lately, his focus has shifted to large language models, specifically a persistent issue known as hallucination, which is when an artificial intelligence model lacks the correct facts but confidently invents an answer anyway.
* [What sports cars can teach us about optimizing AI spend:](https://cloud.google.com/transform/gemini-enterprise-optimize-ai-token-spend?e=48754805) More tokens doesn't always mean better AI. Read our conversation with Mike Clark, Director of Product Management for Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, on how to balance horsepower with efficiency and get the highest return out of every dollar you spend on AI.

### **News you can use:**

Looking for a steer on your foundation or inspiration for your next project? Take a look at some of our favorite how-to guides from August: 

* [10 questions every startup should answer before moving to production with their AI prototype](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/10-questions-for-your-startup-developers?e=48754805): These ten are scoped to the prototype-to-production transition itself. Each question ends with a short, runnable snippet you can copy into your own project today. Adjacent decisions that matter just as much but aren't specific to that move, your data layer and RAG architecture, CI/CD, network design, are deliberately out of frame here.
* [Your chance to start building AI agents from the absolute basics](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/your-chance-to-start-building-ai-agents-from-the-absolute-basics?e=48754805): Agent Valley is a free, 5-week live learning series designed to take you from scratch to building your very own hands-on agent systems. And instead of staring at boring terminal lines, you’ll be building and playing inside a tiny, low-poly virtual world!

Stay tuned for monthly updates on Google Cloud’s AI announcements, news, and best practices. For a deeper dive into the latest from Google Cloud customers, read our monthly recap, [Cool stuff customers built.](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/customers/cool-stuff-google-cloud-customers-built-monthly-round-up?e=48754805)

## July

Since launching the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform a few months ago, we’ve watched businesses move from basic experiments to serious, production-grade builds. We want to make it even easier — and more secure — for you to scale those systems.

Along with a batch of new platform updates, this month we’ve put together 13 practical demos and 20 diagnostic questions to help your engineering teams align on a strong architectural blueprint. Let’s dive in! 

### **Top announcements**

* [What’s new in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/whats-new-in-gemini-enterprise-agent-platform?e=48754805): In this helpful recap, we announced some of our most popular capabilities are available for everyone, from Agent Runtime to Agent Identity.
* [Now in preview: Find and fix software vulnerabilities with CodeMender](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/find-and-fix-software-vulnerabilities-with-codemender?e=48754805): As adversarial AI threats accelerate attacks on code, security teams must counter them with machine-speed defenses that can automate code remediation and fight AI with AI. You can learn more about CodeMender and review the documentation [here](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/codemender).
* [Solve harder problems with AlphaEvolve, now available to everyone on Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/alphaevolve-is-available-for-everyone?e=48754805): AlphaEvolve is a code optimization and discovery agent built on top of Gemini that helps solve the hardest algorithmic problems and achieve breakthroughs for your business and research.

### **Thought leadership (editor’s pick):**

If automation requires delegation, then delegation requires trust. But letting an AI agent run on its own is a big leap for any business. While the productivity gains are clear, the fear of losing control is very real. This month, we sat down with our experts to discuss how leaders can navigate this shift by focusing on transparency, predictability, and setting clear boundaries for how agents handle weird data exceptions.

Here’s our picks for the month to learn more.

* [How leaders can scale AI by trading control for trust (Q&A)](https://cloud.google.com/transform/scale-ai-by-trading-control-for-trust?e=48754805): We sat down with Michael Gerstenhaber, VP of Product Management for Gemini Enterprise, to discuss why the future of AI is about defining safe boundaries.
* [What makes an AI agent trustworthy](https://cloud.google.com/transform/what-makes-an-ai-agent-trustworthy-data-cloud?e=48754805): Context is fast becoming one of the most valuable assets a company owns. Prajakta Damle, Senior Director, Product Management, shares what it takes to get trustworthy AI right.

### **News you can use:**

What if you’re looking for a steer on your basic foundation, inspiration for recipes, or some inspiration? Take a look at some of our favorite how-to guides from July: 

* [Automate your agent development lifecycle using any coding agent](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/automate-agent-development-lifecycles-with-gemini-enterprise?e=48754805): Stuck prototyping? With Agents CLI skills, you can go through the different phases of the entire agent lifecycle without ever leaving your coding agent.
* [Why AI apps fail in production (And how Google solved it)](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/why-ai-apps-fail-in-production?e=48754805): Only 5% of AI prototypes make it to production, and the other 95% fall into the validation abyss. How can you move confidently into production?
* [13 hands-on demos to build on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/13-demos-on-gemini-enterprise-agent-platform?e=48754805): Not sure where to start with Agent Platform? Here’s 13 ways you can stir up some creativity.

Stay tuned for monthly updates on Google Cloud’s AI announcements, news, and best practices. For a deeper dive into the latest from Google Cloud customers, read our monthly recap, [Cool stuff customers built.](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/customers/cool-stuff-google-cloud-customers-built-monthly-round-up?e=48754805)

---

## June

Our main focus in June was helping your teams build, scale, and secure AI. Today, we’re sharing a fresh roundup of updates designed to help you run smarter, more secure applications while keeping everything under your control. 

We even shared a cool virtual shopping demo at Cannes to show how retailers can make product discovery more exciting. Let’s dive in! 

### **Top announcements**

* [Introducing the Open Knowledge Format](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/how-the-open-knowledge-format-can-improve-data-sharing?e=48754805): We introduced the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), an open specification that formalizes the LLM-wiki pattern into a portable, interoperable format. This is a vendor-neutral, agent- and human-friendly standard for representing the metadata, context, and curated knowledge that modern AI systems need.
* [Collaboration with Apple on its expanded Private Cloud Compute (PCC) systems](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/powering-the-next-era-of-confidential-ai?e=48754805): Our collaboration with Apple is built on a foundation of deep commitment to privacy that leverages Google Cloud's security and privacy technologies. At the heart of this collaboration is our Confidential Computing portfolio and our Titanium security architecture.
* [Claude Fable 5: Available on Google Cloud:](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/cloud-fable-5-on-google-cloud?e=48754805) Claude Fable 5, Anthropic’s latest frontier model, is now generally available on Google Cloud. This launch is the latest proof point of our ongoing commitment to bring the industry's latest models straight to our Agent Platform.
* [Cloud Atelier: How Gemini Enterprise is helping restyle the retail playbook](https://cloud.google.com/transform/gemini-enterprise-is-helping-restyle-the-retail-playbook?e=48754805): This year at Cannes, we showcased Cloud Atelier — a destination-based, virtual shopping experience that highlights how retail brands can turn this classic dilemma into an exciting moment of product discovery.

### **Thought leadership (editor’s pick):**

* [How Google Cloud Security uses AI internally](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/cloud-ciso-perspectives-how-google-cloud-security-uses-ai-internally?e=48754805): To counter machine-speed, AI-driven threats, we’ve worked hard to transition Google Cloud’s security posture to an autonomous, proactive model. By embedding specialized AI agents directly into our software development lifecycle (SDLC), we’ve created automated guardrails that protect code at a scale and speed unreachable by human teams — and we’re taking steps to make those same guardrails widely available.
* [The 4 lessons that guided AI Threat Defense](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/cloud-ciso-perspectives-the-4-lessons-that-guided-ai-threat-defense?e=48754805): We introduced Chris Betz as the new CISO of Google Cloud. For his first Cloud CISO Perspectives, Chris shares four key lessons we learned about using AI to the defender’s advantage while building AI Threat Defense.

### **News you can use:**

* [5 lessons from red teaming AI applications:](https://cloud.google.com/transform/5-lessons-from-red-teaming-ai-applications?e=48754805) To help you build AI securely, Mandiant has developed a proactive, risk-based approach centered on the Good AI Assessment (GAIA) Top 10, outlined in our new report, Secure Development of Generative AI Applications: A Proactive Approach.
* [How to unlock true ROI in software development – a deep dive into the latest DORA research:](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/how-to-measure-the-business-value-of-generative-ai?e=48754805) To help you evaluate the costs and business benefits of AI, we recently shared the DORA: ROI of AI-assisted software development report. This research offers a practical approach to help your team work through early adoption challenges, align engineering plans, and drive business growth.
* [Agent Factory Recap: 100X engineering with AI agents in Google Antigravity 2.0](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/developers-practitioners/agent-factory-recap-100x-engineering-with-ai-agents-in-google-antigravity-20?e=48754805): In this episode of the Agent Factory, Shir Meir Lador, Head of AI Engineering, Google Cloud Developer Relations, sat down with Rody Davis, one of Google’s top agentic engineers. They dive into the massive shift from traditional IDEs to agent-first platforms, the reality of code reviews in an AI-driven world, and how to use "skills" to perform at a 100X level.

Stay tuned for monthly updates on Google Cloud’s AI announcements, news, and best practices. For a deeper dive into the latest from Google Cloud customers, read our monthly recap, [Cool stuff customers built.](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/customers/cool-stuff-google-cloud-customers-built-monthly-round-up?e=48754805)

---

## May

We’ve had a busy month! Between announcing Gemini Spark and Gemini 3.5 at Google I/O – and unveiling Google AI Threat Defense, our latest AI-powered cybersecurity solution, we had a lot to share with Google Cloud customers. Keeping up with the latest news takes time, so we gathered the most important announcements, thought leadership, and technical guides in one place to help you quickly catch up.

To learn more about our I/O announcements, here’s [everything you need to know](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/innovations-from-google-io-26-on-google-cloud?e=48754805) for Google Cloud customers, and [top news for startups](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/startups/startup-news-from-io-and-what-it-means-to-founders?e=48754805).

### **Top announcements**

**Introducing Google AI Threat Defense to help you outpace the adversary:** Google Cloud is introducing a comprehensive AI-powered cybersecurity solution — Google AI Threat Defense — an always-on autonomous security platform. Learn more [here](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/introducing-google-ai-threat-defense?e=48754805).

+ **Gemini 3.5:** Our latest family of models combines frontier intelligence with action – starting with Gemini 3.5 Flash.
+ **Gemini Omni:** Our new model is a leap forward in world understanding, multimodality, and editing, letting you generate any output from any input, starting with video.
+ **Google Antigravity:** Google Antigravity’s expanded capabilities and new integration with Agent Platform bring agentic development to your entire organization.
+ **Gemini Spark:** For Gemini Enterprise and Workspace customers, Gemini Spark is your 24/7 personal AI agent that helps you work more efficiently by autonomously taking action on your behalf, under your direction.
+ **Google Workspace:** Google Pics, our new image generation and editing tool, and new voice features in Gmail, Docs and Keep, help reimagine how you work.

* **Agent Designer** uses the same no-code agent designer experience of Agent Platform and lets employees build sophisticated schedule- and trigger-based agents using any enterprise connector. It gives you a virtual flowchart of your agent, allowing you to inspect, test, and approve workflows, ensuring total transparency for executing critical business processes.
* **Long-running agents** aredesigned to execute complex business processes. They can work autonomously in secure cloud sandboxes, giving agents the ability to orchestrate business logic, write code to build custom tools, and complete multi-step work like reconciliation activities or sales prospect sequencing — without needing constant prompting.

* **Projects** create a dedicated space where the agent’s memory is confined to the files and conversations your team adds. By connecting it to data sources including Google Drive, NotebookLM, and Google Group Chats, the agent becomes an expert on a specific topic and can provide team members daily briefings or status updates without digging through months of documents.
* **Skills** create simple shortcuts using an “@” mention for repetitive tasks such as applying brand guidelines, formatting a report, and accessing specific data.
* **Canvas** gives our customers an interactive editor directly within Gemini Enterprise. It allows teams to easily create and edit Docs and Slides, and even export to Microsoft 365 files, within the same experience.

These integrations enable your agents to retrieve data and execute tasks with your systems-of-record.

**3. AI Hypercomputer:** Designed specifically for demanding AI workloads, our AI Hypercomputer is an advanced, purpose-built architecture that unites performance-optimized hardware for compute, storage, networking, open software and machine learning frameworks — as well as flexible consumption models — into a single, integrated system. We are [announcing](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/compute/ai-infrastructure-at-next26) innovations at every layer of the AI Hypercomputer:

* **TPU 8t, optimized for training,** uses breakthrough Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) technology to scale up to 9,600 TPUs and 2 PB of shared, high-bandwidth memory in a single superpod. It achieves 3x the processing power of Ironwood and delivers up to 2x more performance/Watt.
* **TPU 8i, optimized for inference,** uses our new Boardfly topology to directly connect 1,152 TPUs in a single pod. It features 3x more on-chip SRAM compared to previous versions to host larger KV caches entirely on-silicon and integrates a specialized Collectives Acceleration Engine. Taken together, TPU 8i delivers 80% better performance per dollar for inference than the prior generation, [enabling millions of concurrent agents to run cost-effectively](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/compute/tpu-8t-and-tpu-8i-technical-deep-dive).

**4. The Agentic Data Cloud:** A new data architecture built for the speed and scale of agentic AI. The Agentic Data Cloud delivers an AI-native architecture, allowing agents to perceive, reason, and act on your behalf in real-time, including: 

* **Cross-Cloud Lakehouse,** standardized on Apache Iceberg, is our Lakehouse that enables you to leave your data in AWS or Azure (coming later this year) while querying it instantly — without the friction of vendor lock-in or the cost of data movement
* **Knowledge Catalog** constructs a unified, dynamic context graph of your entire business enabling you to ground agents in all of your business data and semantics. With Smart Storage and the Object Context API, files in Google Cloud Storage are instantly tagged and enriched with metadata before an agent touches them. Then our Knowledge Engine uses Gemini to autonomously tag, define logic and instantly map complex relationships across your entire enterprise, providing the semantic definition your agents have been missing.

Protecting the agentic enterprise: Security built for the AI era.** Our full-stack AI approach, from the chips to the models, gives you a competitive advantage with better integration and velocity to help protect customers. ## Janurary

We used to have to learn the language of computers. In 2026, they’re learning ours.

We kicked off the year by exploring the future of agentic commerce, where AI agents navigate the web to find and buy products for us. Our leaders call this the "[invisible shelf](https://cloud.google.com/transform/the-invisible-shelf-retail-cpg-agentic-commerce-how-to?e=48754805)" — a world where commerce isn't tied to a specific website. To make this reality scalable, we announced the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), a shared language that allows agents and retailers to understand each other. 

We brought that same fluency to our creative and technical tools:

1. Updates to Veo 3.1 allow creators to use simple inputs — like reference images — to generate precise, mobile-ready video.
2. Natural language queries: With Comments to SQL in BigQuery, we’re removing the language barrier to data. Engineers can now write queries by describing their intent in natural language, prioritizing the question over the code.

Let’s dive in.

### Top hits

1. [**Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience (CX):**](https://www.googlecloudpresscorner.com/2026-01-11-Google-Cloud-Brings-Shopping-and-Customer-Service-Together-with-Gemini-Enterprise-for-Customer-Experience)Specifically built for agentic retail, this platform transforms fragmented search, commerce and service touch points into one seamless journey — whether you need a shopping assistant, a support bot, agentic search or help with merchandising. 

2. [**We announced Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP):**](https://developers.googleblog.com/under-the-hood-universal-commerce-protocol-ucp/)A new open standard for agentic commerce that works across the entire shopping journey — from discovery and buying to post-purchase support. UCP establishes a common language for agents and systems to operate together across consumer surfaces, businesses and payment providers. So instead of requiring unique connections for every individual agent, UCP enables all agents to interact easily. UCP is built to work across verticals and is compatible with existing industry protocols like Agent2Agent (A2A), Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) and Model Context Protocol (MCP).

3. [**We updated Veo 3.1, including improvements to Ingredients to Video and Portrait mode:**](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/veo-3-1-ingredients-to-video/)Veo is getting more expressive, with improvements that help you create more fun, creative, high-quality videos based on ingredient images, built directly for the mobile format. This includes:

* Improvements to Veo 3.1 Ingredients to Video, our capability that lets you create videos based on reference images.
* Native vertical outputs for Ingredients to Video (portrait mode) to power mobile-first, short-form video creation.
* State-of-the-art upscaling to 1080p and 4K resolution 1 for high-fidelity production workflows.

These updates are launching in the Gemini app, YouTube, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini API and Vertex AI.

4. [**Vibe querying with comments-to-SQL:**](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/vibe-querying-with-comments-to-sql-in-bigquery?e=48754805) Crafting complex SQL queries can be challenging. This feature makes writing queries using natural language – ‘vibe querying’ – a reality. entries.title: Despite years of rain, Blue Mountains forests still haven’t recovered from the Black Summer megafires
entries.content:
![](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756926/original/file-20260831-50-6srhxj.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&rect=2%2C0%2C5117%2C3411&q=45&auto=format&w=1050&h=700&fit=crop)

[Brook Mitchell/Getty](https://www.gettyimages.com.au/detail/news-photo/general-view-of-fire-damaged-country-in-the-the-greater-news-photo/1207725182?adppopup=true)

For three years before the Black Summer megafires of 2019–20, cool season rainfall in southeastern Australia was [only half](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adj3460) that of normal. When fires broke out, intensely dry conditions helped them spread through areas typically resistant to burning, such as wetlands and [rainforests](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21266-5).

After the fires came [three years](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023GL106939) of above-average rainfall, and [scientific reports](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2022.113087) charted rapid vegetation regrowth.

It’s easy to think the rains let nature repair itself. But is that the full story? In our [new research](https://doi.org/10.1111/gcb.71057), we looked at what happened to seven severely burnt plant communities in the Greater Blue Mountains, west of Sydney.

We found a mixed picture. Wet sclerophyll forests supporting tall eucalypts skirted by ferns recovered within five years. But Blue Mountains rainforests did not recover from burns of any severity. Nor did grassy woodlands.

## How can we track recovery?

To find out how well forests and other communities recovered from the Black Summer fires, we tracked recovery across the million-hectare Greater Blue Mountains [World Heritage Area](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/917). Seven severe fires hit this region over the 2019–20 summer. The biggest was the Gospers Mountain fire, which burned an area [seven times](https://www.smh.com.au/national/nsw/the-monster-a-short-history-of-australia-s-biggest-forest-fire-20191218-p53l4y.html) the size of Singapore – the largest fire from a single ignition point in Australia’s recorded history.

Five years on, if you had looked out across the Blue Mountains landscape you might have thought recovery was well under way. Thick scrub quickly replaced charred undergrowth in many areas. Across our study sites, many burned regions had denser understoreys – the layer of vegetation between forest floor and canopy – than unburnt areas.

But recovery isn’t just about how much vegetation is there. It’s about whether the layers of shrubs and canopy trees that make up a functioning plant community have returned to their previous state.

After fire moves through, some plant species rapidly regrow, outcompeting their rivals for light and water. But these species are often short-lived, failing to survive beyond a few years. On the other hand, species such as eucalypts and [banksia](https://search.informit.org/doi/abs/10.3316/INFORMIT.279457321556936) may take years to regrow but then live much longer.

This means depending on when we take our measurements, we might mistake a temporary pulse of growth for real recovery.

To address this issue, our study tracked plant [growth](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2022.113151) using a time-series of satellite images. This way, we could see the full trajectory of recovery, not just a snapshot.

A plant community that has fully recovered from burns will look stable year to year and mirror patterns of growth at unburnt sites. Poorly recovered areas, in contrast, will show distinct fluctuations.

We used this method to track recovery from low- to extreme-severity fire at 760 forest, heath and wetland sites in the Greater Blue Mountains region.

## What did we find?

An earlier [large-scale synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08174-6) two years after the Black Summer fires found wet forests had suffered greater declines than drier plant communities.

Our findings five years after the fires tell a more complex story.

Some wet forests, such as wet sclerophyll, were able to take advantage of the heavy rains to recover fully within five years.

Others were less fortunate. The Blue Mountains are home to rare remnant rainforest, featuring stands of trees such as coachwood, lilly-pilly and sassafras, whose ancestors date back to [Gondwana](https://bmnature.info/veg-rainforest.shtml). We found these had not recovered after fires of any severity.

The region’s grassy woodlands also showed no sign of recovery when burned, despite being dry, open areas.

Why? We suggest the intense rains following Black Summer made it difficult for the community’s characteristic grasses and tussocks – adapted to dry conditions – to successfully re-establish.

## What if the big dry hadn’t ended?

The years of heavy rain after the Black Summer fires were unusual. If drought had continued, would we have seen different recovery outcomes?

To tease out this question, we modelled what recovery would have looked like for plant communities under drought stress.

Simply put, all would be worse off. In particular, wet sclerophyll forests and freshwater wetlands showed declines five times greater than other plant communities.

This is likely due to the fact that the plant species in these ecosystems need heavy rainfall to re-establish. For instance, freshwater wetlands often need to be [completely flooded](https://doi.org/10.1071/MF24040) for species to return.

These communities may be pushed to the point of collapse if drought persists after the next megafire.

## What can we do?

Ferocious fires have swept through [Europe](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-02/europe-fires-fingerprints-of-climate-change/106967040) in recent months and the southern summer is likely to coincide with a [strong El Niño event](https://theconversation.com/how-will-this-years-record-breaking-el-nino-affect-nz-and-the-world-5-things-to-know-290159), bringing a higher risk of intense heatwaves, drought and fire.

As climate change accelerates, these extreme conditions will become more common. To protect our plant communities, we must tailor our fire-management strategies. No two communities respond to fire the same way, and recovery outcomes differ greatly depending on whether post-fire conditions are hot and dry or cool and wet. A one-size-fits-all approach won’t work.

During the Black Summer fires, a team of firefighters protected the [last wild stand](https://www.smh.com.au/environment/conservation/dinosaur-trees-survived-black-summer-but-they-haven-t-recovered-enough-for-the-next-bushfire-20210113-p56tty.html) of the ancient, fire-averse Wollemi pine in the Blue Mountains.

To help rainforests and other fire-averse plant communities survive, we will need technologies that help us rapidly detect and suppress new fires – and [long-term monitoring](https://www.nespthreatenedspecies.edu.au/news-and-media/media-releases/we-need-to-know-the-critical-role-of-monitoring-in-australia-s-fight-against-extinctions) programs to let us know when species are at risk.

In other landscapes, we must rethink our reliance on [fuel-reduction burns](https://theconversation.com/does-fuel-reduction-burning-help-prevent-damage-from-fires-11600). This is because plants are at higher risk of damage from fire if they have been frequently [burnt in the past](https://theconversation.com/catastrophic-declines-massive-data-haul-reveals-why-so-many-plants-and-animals-suffer-after-fire-241691). When we repeatedly burn an area, we [inflate this risk](https://theconversation.com/in-1939-a-royal-commission-found-burning-forests-leads-to-more-bushfires-but-this-cycle-of-destruction-can-be-stopped-269099) and condemn many plants and animals to staggering losses in future fires.

Of course, all these efforts won’t matter if we fail to tackle the underlying reason why fires are getting more frequent and severe – [climate change](https://stateofwildfires.com/latest-report/).

![The Conversation](https://counter.theconversation.com/content/290432/count.gif)

*Emily Simpson receives funding from the Ecological Society of Australia.*

*Aaron Greenville receives funding from the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water.*

*Glenda Wardle receives funding from the Australian Research Council and the Terrestrial Ecosystem Research Network. She is a WWF-Australia director and a member of the Australasian Network for Plant Conservation.*

*Chris Dickman does not work for, consult, own shares in or receive funding from any company or organisation that would benefit from this article, and has disclosed no relevant affiliations beyond their academic appointment.*

entries.title: 10 Apple Health Hacks Every iPhone User Should Know
entries.content:
We may earn a commission from links on this page.

Even if you’ve never opened the Apple Health app, if you have an iPhone, you’ve probably used apps that send information to its on-phone database. Apple Health is a powerful tool for controlling who gets access to your health data, logging data in different ways, and even taking at-home screening tests for certain health issues. If you [have an Apple Watch](https://lifehacker.com/health/fitness-hacks-every-apple-watch-user-should-know), that’s great, but you don’t need one (or any wearable!) to take advantage of most of these 10 hacks to get more out of the Apple Health app.

## Lock down (or open up) your privacy controls

Before we get into the other hacks, I’d like to discuss just how private your Apple Health data is (or isn’t). Apple provides its Health privacy policy [here](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/health-app/ "open in a new window"), and it says that your data lives on your own device and is encrypted when your phone is locked. There are some exceptions, though, which you can turn on or off. Here are the main things you may want to check on:

* Individual apps can ask for permission to read data from Apple Health. (They also need your permission to write data to it.) You can control per-app permissions in Settings. Or, for a specific data point (like “walking and running distance”), go to that area of Apple Health and tap **Data Sources and Access**.
* You can back up your health data via iCloud, which means it will live on Apple’s servers so you can access it from any of your devices. It is encrypted so Apple cannot read it. Manage this from your iCloud settings (in Settings, under your name).
* You can share health data with your doctor or with people you know, like family members. To manage who has access, go to the Health app and tap the **Sharing** tab.
* During workouts, some data from your workout may appear in a Live Activity widget on your lock screen. To hide this data while your phone is locked, go to the Settings app, tap **Face ID & Passcode**, and then under **Allow Access When Locked**, toggle **Workout Health Data**.
* Your Medical ID may be available when your device is locked. (This is how bystanders and first responders can access your emergency contact or other information you’d like to remain available in emergencies.) To control access to this, go to the Health app, find **Medical ID**, and toggle **Show When Locked**.

## Set up tracking so you never forget to take your medication

The Health app includes a built-in medication tracker with a number of hidden features. Browse or search for **Medications**, and set up tracking by adding a medication, or anything else. You can type in the name, or use your camera to scan the bottle’s label. (This also works for over-the-counter meds and supplements, like if you want to be sure to take a vitamin every day.) I like that you can customize a pill-shaped icon to match a pill’s appearance.

Next, you can set up reminders. From this screen, you can tell the app when you plan to take your medication (if it’s one you take regularly, rather than as needed). The Health app will notify you at that time. To make the most of this feature, I recommend setting up follow-up reminders, which you’ll find on a different screen as well—more about that below.

After you set up your medications, scroll to the bottom of the medications screen and tap **Pin to Summary**. Now you just have to open the Health app and tap Medications to see a list of what you need to take today. You can also log via Siri, including batched logging like “Siri, log that I took my 10 a.m. meds” so you don’t have to list each one.

At the bottom of the Medications screen, you can tap **Options** and turn on **Follow Up Reminders**, which will give you an extra notification 30 minutes after the first one if you haven’t logged a dose. I use this feature all the time myself: I get the first reminder while I’m in the middle of doing something, eventually take the pill, then the follow-up reminds me to log it. If I got distracted along the way, I have a second chance to not miss a dose.

Another handy feature here is the **Export PDF** button at the bottom of the page, which will print out a list of all your current medications so you can bring it to your medical appointments or anywhere else you need to.

## Customize the home screen to find any health data quickly

If you’re not familiar with the Health app, you might not think there’s much there—just a few things on the home screen. You can change that, but it takes a few steps. You see, rather than being a minimalist app, there’s *so much* available in Health that Apple figures it’s not worth giving you a big list to start off. Tap the magnifying glass icon in the lower right corner, and you’ll see a whole list of categories. You can search from this screen, or browse the categories.

Definitely take a minute to browse through these and see what features you might actually use. If you track what you eat in an Apple Health-connected app, you’ll be able to see all the individual components here: how much protein you’ve gotten today, for instance. Anything that a wearable can track is on here, including things you probably didn’t realize. I have a grade for my walking steadiness, for example.

Once you’ve figured out which of these hundreds of data points are actually useful, put the ones you care about on the main app screen (called **Summary**). Find a relevant card by searching or browsing, scroll to the bottom, and tap **Pin to Summary**. This way you can see exactly what you want when you open the app: say, your steps, protein intake, and the day’s medications. (Plus a few things you may want to add after you learn about them below...)

## Track your menstrual cycle without risking your privacy

A lot of us are nervous about logging reproductive health data anywhere that may not be private. I’ve written that Euki may be the [best standalone app for privacy,](https://lifehacker.com/health/euki-period-tracking-app) but you don’t need to use an app at all: Tracking directly in Apple Health means that your data is encrypted and lives on your phone, subject to the privacy features discussed above.

To use the built-in tracker, go to the magnifying glass and tap (or search for) **Cycle Tracking**. The cycle tracker on this screen (which you can pin to your summary) allows you to log menstrual bleeding, as well as “factors” like contraceptive use, pregnancy, and more.

Under the **Options** at the bottom of this screen, you can turn on period predictions, fertile window estimates, and more. I recommend enabling the **Symptoms** log if you’d like to keep track of things like cramps and nausea. You can also decide if you want Apple Health to use your temperature and heart rate data from a wearable for better cycle detection.

## Track your mental health over time

Another surprising use for manual logging in the Health app is under **Mental Wellbeing**. This is a really useful screen, since it collects things known to affect mental health, like your sleep, exercise minutes, time in daylight, and more. From here, you can also set up emotion and mood logging. The app explains that it considers emotions to be how you feel right now, and moods are how you’ve felt overall that day.

You can turn on reminders to log your moods. The default is to log twice per day: once around midday, and once at the end of the day. Scroll to the bottom of the **Mental Wellbeing** screen to set up logging.  Once you’ve set it up, it will appear as **State of Mind**; you may want to pin this to your summary. You can even view graphs of your state of mind over time, and see what other factors they associate with. A really useful view is to tap **Show in Charts** and then highlight **Life Factors** so you can see if your moods seem to track your exercise minutes or your hours of sleep.

## Take a hearing test (if you have AirPods Pro 2 or 3)

The Health app also includes a built-in hearing test, but it requires [AirPods Pro 3](https://zdcs.link/aN55nB?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=AirPods%20Pro%203&object_type=content&short_url=aN55nB&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") (or AirPods Pro 2). To find the hearing test, look up **Hearing** in the Health app, then **Get More From Health**, and then **Take Hearing Test**. This will only be available if you have the right type of headphones connected. Follow the prompts to take the test. Apple has more information on this test [here](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120991 "open in a new window"). If your results seem concerning, you can export a PDF of your results to discuss with a professional.

## Find your medical records without having to go through a patient portal

Accessing your medical records through patient portals can be annoying. Instead, you can import your digital medical records directly into the Health app, giving you quick access to your medical history as needed. [Apple offers a list](https://institutions.healthrecords.apple.com/ "open in a new window") of the healthcare systems whose data it can access.

It’s worth looking over the [privacy policies](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111755 "open in a new window") for this feature as well, but the good news is that the data follows an encrypted connection between your phone and the healthcare organization, without ever giving Apple (the company) access to it. I’d recommend turning off **Improve Health Records**, which sends an anonymized version of your data to Apple; health records are detailed information about your body—but feel free to leave it on if that’s your preference. You can back up your health data over iCloud, as discussed above.

## Track your blood pressure, even if you don’t have a device that estimates it

As with menstrual cycle tracking, it can be useful to any health data directly in the app. You can actually do this with just about any data point: just view that type of data, and then tap the **plus sign** in the upper right corner. Think you took about 1,000 steps when you had your watch off? Just tap the plus on the Steps screen and add them.

A handy place to use this feature is for blood pressure tracking. Some wearables estimate your blood pressure, like [Whoop](https://lifehacker.com/health/fda-says-whoops-blood-pressure-feature-is-illegal) and the [Samsung Galaxy Watch](https://lifehacker.com/health/samsung-galaxy-measure-blood-pressure-in-us). But you don’t need one of those to log your numbers: just take note of your blood pressure at the doctor’s office, or when you use a wrist cuff or one of those machines they sometimes have at pharmacies. Open **Blood Pressure** and tap the **plus**, then put in the new reading. You’ll be able to view your history of blood pressure readings, and even see charts of how it has changed over time.

## Get a better cardio fitness estimate by entering your medications

Some medications affect your heart rate, most notably beta blockers and calcium channel blockers. If you’re taking one of those, your heart rate won’t match Apple’s general-purpose formulas for gauging your cardio fitness (a [VO2max](https://lifehacker.com/what-is-vo2max) estimate) from your heart rate. You’ll appear to have a higher cardio fitness than you actually have.

To let Apple account for this, go to your profile picture, tap **Health Details**, tap **Edit** at the top of the page, and scroll down to **Medications That Affect Heart Rate**. You can select calcium channel blockers or beta blockers, or both; these are the only categories of medication that Apple can account for.

## Automatically share medical info in an emergency

There’s a Medical ID feature that can be accessed from your lock screen even without unlocking your phone. It’s a great place to put your emergency contact information, but to make the most use of it, you need the people in your life to know how to access the information and what’s in there.

I first learned about the Medical ID when I was teaching a class. A student came up to tell me about a medical condition, and showed me how to access her Medical ID (it’s right at the bottom of the lock screen). Most importantly, she made sure I knew what information I’d be able to find there, so I knew *when* and *whether* to reach for it in an emergency.

I’d advise that you do the same if you want to be prepared. Besides allergies and contact information, the Medical ID field can include information on whether you’re pregnant, what medications you take, any medical conditions you’d like to disclose, and your height, weight, and blood type. There’s also an area at the bottom for notes, where you can add any information you feel is critical.

Also consider whether you want to turn on **Share During Emergency Call**, which allows this information to be shared with emergency services. You can also control whether or not your Medical ID appears on your lock screen using a separate toggle.

Nintendo’s price increase officially took effect today, Sept. 1, raising the Switch 2’s U.S. MSRP from $449.99 to $499.99. That means Woot’s refurbished console is now approximately 20% cheaper than buying a new one at its revised price, and even $50 below its former price. If you’ve been waiting for one of the better [Labor Day gaming deals](https://lifehacker.com/labor-day), this may be among your last opportunities to get the console for less than $400. The promotion is currently scheduled to end at 11:59 p.m. CT on Sept. 25, but Woot’s inventory is limited, so this offer may disappear sooner if it sells out. Purchases are limited to one console per customer.

The biggest consideration is that this isn’t a new or Nintendo-certified refurbished unit. According to Woot, its Grade A designation means the console has been inspected, passed a complete diagnostic test, and is guaranteed to have minimal cosmetic damage with like-new functionality. It’s also covered under Woot’s [90-day-limited-warranty](https://electronics.woot.com/warranty "open in a new window"), though that’s shorter than the warranty you would ordinarily receive with a brand new console

The console, which only ships to the 48 contiguous states in the U.S., arrives in a generic white or brown box, but includes its original equipment: the Switch 2 dock, two Joy-Con 2 controllers, Joy-Con grip and straps, AC adapter, USB-C charging cable, and Ultra High Speed HDMI cable. Amazon Prime members qualify for free standard shipping.

The Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch 1080p LCD touchscreen with HDR and refresh rates up to 120 fps, plus 256GB of internal storage. Its dock supports resolutions up to 4K when connected to a compatible TV. It also plays compatible physical and digital games from the original Switch, although some titles may have limitations.

You might be focused on the best Amazon Labor Day deals, but don’t overlook Woot: It’s owned by Amazon and frequently runs short-lived discounts that undercut prices on Amazon itself, especially on refurbished tech. This [Grade A refurbished Nintendo Switch 2](https://zdcs.link/z7GGxn?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Grade%20A%20refurbished%20Nintendo%20Switch%202&object_type=content&short_url=z7GGxn&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window")  is easily one of the best Labor Day tech deals for Nintendo Switch fans willing to accept refurbished hardware and a shorter warranty.

And if you’re comparing other forms of immersive gaming before spending $400, here’s how the [Meta Quest 3 compares with the Quest 3S](https://lifehacker.com/tech/which-is-better-meta-quest-3-vs-meta-quest-3s).

---

## When is Labor Day 2026?

Labor Day falls on Monday, September 7, 2026. The holiday is always observed on the first Monday in September, though sales can extend before and after the holiday.

## When are Labor Day sales?

Labor Day sales commonly begin in late August and continue through Labor Day weekend. Some retailers extend their promotions into the following week, while individual deals may end sooner or sell out. This Woot Switch 2 offer is scheduled to run through September 25 at 11:59 p.m. CT unless inventory sells out first.

## Are Labor Day deals better than Black Friday?

Not universally. Black Friday normally delivers a wider selection of tech discounts, but Labor Day can be competitive for gaming equipment, TVs, laptops and outgoing models. Waiting for Black Friday could produce a better price, but there’s no guarantee this particular refurbished console will remain available or that new Switch 2 consoles will fall below their recently increased MSRP.

## Which retailer has the best Labor Day deals overall?

Amazon typically has one of the broadest selections, while Walmart and Best Buy are strong for TVs, computers and gaming products. However, the best retailer depends on the item. Amazon-owned Woot is particularly worth checking for refurbished and open-box tech items, as demonstrated by this Switch 2 price beating the console’s new MSRP by $100.

entries.title: OpenAI Astra: All about the quantum math-solving model with critical hacking skills
entries.content:
![the openai logo appears on a smartphone screen](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06NOXrYA9PutPDr5COAAGVN/hero-image.jpg)

Do you understand quantum parallel repetition? What about quantum complexity, lattice cryptography, or extremal combinatorics?

The new [OpenAI](https://mashable.com/category/openai) model Astra knows all about them.

On Aug. 1, OpenAI [confirmed the existence of Astra](https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/), calling it "our next major model." And on Sept. 1, [OpenAI confirmed in a blog post](https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/) that Astra has reached a "critical" cyber threat level, but that it will also be "available soon." For safety reasons, the company plans to restrict its most advanced cybersecurity capabilities to a closed group of select testing partners.

## Everything we know about the OpenAI Astra model

We first learned about Astra when OpenAI announced that a mysterious new model had made some notable breakthroughs in research-level mathematics.

On Aug. 1, the ChatGPT-maker revealed that an internal model named Astra had solved 10 major open math problems, some of which had been unresolved for decades. Then, on Aug. 7, OpenAI announced that [Astra had developed such advanced cyber capabilities](https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities/) that new security controls were necessary and that some internal development work would be paused.

At the time, OpenAI said it couldn't "rule out critical cyber capabilities under our [Preparedness Framework](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/18a02b5d-6b67-4cec-ab64-68cdfbddebcd/preparedness-framework-v2.pdf)," meaning the model could have existential-threat-level cybersecurity capabilities. (OpenAI's Preparedness Framework tracks risk levels in three categories: biological and chemical, cybersecurity, and AI self-improvement.)

Finally, on Sept. 1, OpenAI confirmed that not only is Astra coming soon, but that it does, in fact, meet the "critical" threshold for cyber capabilities. Previously, OpenAI deemed [GPT-5.6-Sol](https://mashable.com/tech/openai-gpt-56-sol-terra-luna) a "high" cybersecurity risk, making Astra the first OpenAI model to be classified as a genuine "critical" risk.

"Under our Preparedness Framework, a model reaches the Critical cybersecurity threshold if it can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention, or can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets given only a high level desired goal," an OpenAI blog post stated.

## How is OpenAI tightening security around Astra?

Until recently, the prospect of swarms of AI agents conducting relatively autonomous cyber attacks on critical infrastructure was mostly hypothetical. After the [Hugging Face hack](https://mashable.com/tech/hugging-face-openai-rogue-agent-hack-explained), that risk seems much more real. Because of the rapid progress in this domain, some [zero-day bug bounty programs have even been forced to shut down](https://mashable.com/article/ai-discovered-zero-day-bug-reports-crisis) due to the deluge of AI-discovered bugs, as Mashable has reported.

SEE ALSO:
[The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was worse than we thought](https://mashable.com/tech/openai-hugging-face-hack-worse-than-thought)

Back in August, OpenAI tightened sandboxes that keep the Astra model contained and monitored its Chain of Thought to "interrupt high risk activity." In addition, while OpenAI maintains that Astra was not involved in the Hugging Face hack, the company said that "we have incorporated our [learnings](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/67869394-cb91-4c12-888c-5cbd85c7814c/OpenAI-Hugging-Face%20Incident-Technical-Report.pdf) from that incident into our safety approach." OpenAI previously said that it was committed to working with "relevant government agencies and select AI safety organizations to test the capabilities for this model."

Now that the company is readying Astra for release, it's taking additional precautions. When Astra launches, only select testers will have access to its most advanced cybersecurity skills. Eventually, access will be expanded so that it can be used for defensive purposes.

In its [latest blog post](https://openai.com/index/path-to-astra/), OpenAI says its safeguards are built around two objectives:

* **Preventing malicious actors from utilizing the model**
* **Stopping Astra from taking "unauthorized, misaligned actions"**

OpenAI said more safeguarding information will be available when the model launches.

## OpenAI Astra: When is the release date?

We don't know, but OpenAI appears to be actively preparing for its launch, which suggests it's coming very soon. On the same day Anthropic launched Fable 5.1, OpenAI said only that Astra would be "available soon."

At this point, it's unclear if Astra will eventually be released as GPT-5.7, the beginning of GPT-6, or something else entirely.

Major AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have been releasing major updates to their models every few months, with entirely new model families coming out every one to two years. GPT-5 was introduced in August 2025, which means we're due for GPT-6 any time now.

## What else do we know about OpenAI Astra?

The company has also so far declined to answer our questions about Astra, but we'll update this story if we receive more information.

[Bleeping Computer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/artificial-intelligence/openai-teases-astra-its-next-major-ai-model-after-it-solves-10-long-standing-math-problems/) initially described Astra as "a powerful model that allows AI agents to collaborate on different parts of a larger problem." That suggests it's designed for agentic work and can "tackle complex, long-running tasks," also per Bleeping Computer.

We also know that the White House is reportedly close to [finalizing a voluntary AI framework](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/04/technology/white-house-ai-framework.html?eafs_enabled=false) for testing new frontier models like Astra before they're publicly released. And in August, [The Information reported](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/exclusive-openai-previews-astra-ai-model-dc) that OpenAI was actively previewing Astra in Washington, D.C.

[OpenAI's original blog post](https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/) about Astra, "Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science," also made it clear that the new OpenAI model has made significant advances in science and mathematics.

So, we talked to a mathematician about what Astra means for the future of AI and science — and what it doesn't mean.

## New Anthropic and OpenAI models are *really* good at coding and math

![person holds smartphone with openai name and logo on screen](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06NOXrYA9PutPDr5COAAGVN/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788293549.jpg)

Credit: Photographed by Joseph Maldonado / Mashable Composite by Rene Ramos

When Anthropic announced that its unreleased Mythos model was so good at hacking that it was [too dangerous to release](https://mashable.com/article/antropic-pulls-mythos-ai-security-flaws) to the public, [we questioned this narrative](https://mashable.com/article/claude-mythos-preview-project-glasswing-pr-stunt-cybersecurity-experts), as the warning effectively doubled as PR. However, we can't deny that the latest frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI have gotten remarkably good at cybersecurity, agentic coding, and [discovering zero-day bugs](https://mashable.com/article/ai-discovered-zero-day-bug-reports-crisis).

But OpenAI and Anthropic have also shown impressive progress on research-level mathematics.

First, [OpenAI released a disproof](https://openai.com/index/model-disproves-discrete-geometry-conjecture/) of the [Erdős unit distance conjecture](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ErdosUnitDistanceProblem.html) in May. Then, an Anthropic-linked mathematician casually announced that he [used Fable 5 to disprove the Jacobian Conjecture](https://mashable.com/tech/anthropic-fable-5-disproves-jacobian-conjecture), one of the infamous [Smale's problems in mathematics](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SmalesProblems.html). Now, OpenAI has announced that Astra solved 10 more open problems in mathematics.

It's a potentially paradigm-shifting moment, though this is hardly proof that artificial general intelligence or the singularity is nigh.

First, most of these math accomplishments take the form of disproofs and counterexamples, which aren't as impressive as positive proofs that greatly expand our understanding of the universe, like, say, [Andrew Wiles' proof of Fermat's Theorem](https://www.nytimes.com/1993/06/29/science/scientist-at-work-andrew-wiles-math-whiz-who-battled-350-year-old-problem.html).

When Fable 5 disproved the Jacobian Conjecture, I spoke to Columbia professor [Andrew Blumberg](https://cancerdynamics.columbia.edu/andrew-j-blumberg-phd), who is also on the board of directors of [the First Proof project](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/first-proof-is-ais-toughest-math-test-yet-the-results-are-mixed/), which tested the capabilities of frontier large language models in solving research-level mathematics.

At the time, he told me that Fable 5's feat "did not cause me to update my priors about what AI can and can't do." Blumberg added, "This is exactly the kind of thing I would expect AI to be able to do. If there was a counterexample that was concise and easy to state that people haven't found because it's a pain to search through all this stuff, AI will find it."

Ultimately, Blumberg said that Fable 5's counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture didn't necessarily teach us anything new or exciting about the world, even though it was very impressive.

I went back to Blumberg to ask about OpenAI and Astra's latest work, and he said his priors still haven't changed — AI is a very useful tool for advanced science, but Astra's math results don't suggest AI is ready to replace human scientists and mathematicians.

"If you look at what these are, they're pretty short. They are either counterexamples or they are small, extremely clever constructions that build on known things, and it's super cool, right? I want to be clear: If a person had done many of these things, that person would be justly lauded for their achievement, and so [this work is] great, but they don't change my priors."

And, as many people have pointed out (including, most recently, [data scientist Nate Silver](https://x.com/NateSilver538/status/2083754199439835277)), we have to put these results in perspective. While OpenAI was keen to point out that these problems were solved with just $2,000 worth of tokens, that doesn't account for the trillions spent on AI technology in recent years.

"When you hear about the amount of money that's being poured into these machines, and you think about what it would be like if we spent a trillion dollars on hiring and training mathematicians and paying the best mathematicians football players' salaries to do nothing but solve these problems, I think we'd see a shitload of progress," Blumberg told Mashable.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/NateSilver538/status/2083754199439835277 "(Opens in a new tab)")

At the same time, the prospect of Astra-level models being in the hands of every scientist, physicist, and mathematician on Earth is truly exciting. Likewise, the prospect of Astra-like tools being available to hackers and other bad actors is truly concerning.

---

*Disclosure: Ziff Davis, Mashable’s parent company, in April 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.*

entries.title: Dysons $499 squirting AI camera toothbrush proves smart tech has officially gone too far
entries.content:
![two Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrushes on modern bathroom counter](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/hero-image.jpg)

[Dyson](https://mashable.com/category/dyson) just unveiled its latest product: the Dyson CameraJet™, an AI-powered electric toothbrush and water flosser with onboard cameras, priced at $499.99. The smart, app-connected toothbrush-slash-endoscope launches on Sept. 8, but you can pre-order the beauty tech device right now.

The product, with its lightsaber-like hilt and clunky design, sounds to me like an April Fool's Day joke, and I don't know who this is for. The people aren't exactly crying out for $500 toothbushes right now.

[![Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrush](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/product/07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt/hero-image.fill.size_256x256.v1788286900.jpg)](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-image&position=1&element_label=image&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")

[Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrush](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-title&position=1&element_label=Dyson+CameraJet+electric+toothbrush&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")

$499.99
 at Amazon

[Pre-order Here at Amazon](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-button&position=1&element_label=Pre-order+Here+at+Amazon&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)") [Pre-order Here at Dyson](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05u1UqQ5WfhsKP7roMsCqUo&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.dyson.com%2Foral-care%2Felectric-toothbrush%2Fcamerajet%2Fceramic-pink-set&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-button&position=1&element_label=Pre-order+Here+at+Dyson&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=01aUi1nkI6N519XTLoLUNmD&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")

I have to ask: *WTF is going on over at Dyson?*

The English brand is known for its innovative designs. [Dyson's Supersonic hair dryer](https://mashable.com/review/dyson-supersonic-hair-dryer) was truly revolutionary, and I use one almost every day. Dyson is the company that somehow turned boring old [vacuum cleaners](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-dyson-vacuums) into status symbols and [created a futuristic, revolving, hydroponic strawberry farm](https://dysonfarming.com/strawberries/). But in recent years, the company has had some misfires, and anecdotally, they seem to be getting more common. You might remember [the Covid-era Dyson Zone](http://mashable.com/article/dyson-announces-the-dyson-zone), the dystopian headphones with a built-in air purifier. You might also remember [when it was discontinued](https://mashable.com/article/dyson-discontinues-air-purifying-headphones). We also found that the brand's [latest robot vacuums were duds](https://mashable.com/review/dyson-360-vis-nav-robot-vacuum).

![dyson camerajet toothbrush squirts water between teeth](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788287125.jpg)

The Dyson CameraJet™ uses a macro camera and doubles as a dental endoscope.
Credit: Dyson

Perhaps there is a market for Dyson oral care products, but the idea of a toothbrush that uses AI to look into all the nooks and crannies of my mouth and squirt "mouthrinse" into them gives me the heebie-jeebies. Another Mashable editor used the word "nightmare" to describe it.

"
I'm never going to download an app in order to use my toothbrush, and you can't make me.
"

## Introducing the Dyson CameraJet™: What is it?

Dyson says it's been developing the CameraJet electric toothbrush for six years.

The short version: The toothbrush head includes a camera that identifies the gaps between your teeth in real-time and ejects a jet of cleansing water between your teeth to remove plaque.

For the long version, I'll quote the press release:

![close-up portrait of woman using dyson camerajet toothbrush](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-2.fill.size_2000x1500.v1788287125.jpg)

Credit: Dyson

> Today, in Paris, James Dyson revealed an entirely new way to clean your teeth. The Dyson CameraJet™ is the only toothbrush with a camera powered by Gap Optical Targeting™ to identify gaps between teeth and precision-floss while you brush. Gap Optical Targeting™ analyzes 28 live images per second to identify and target gaps between teeth in real time, triggering a precision jet burst of mouthrinse where it is needed.

> It is the result of six years of research, development, and engineering, challenging every aspect of conventional oral care. While others cannot find the gaps between teeth, CameraJet™ can.

## How does the Dyson CameraJet™ electric toothbrush work?

You might think that your mouth is the absolute last place you'd want to place a 100,000-pixel macro lens camera. That is a reasonable thought! The toothbrush uses this camera to analyze 28 images per second. When the toothbrush's software detects a gap between your teeth, the device shoots a jet of water into it within 100 milliseconds. This allows for precision flossing as you brush your teeth.

![the hilt of the dyson camerajet toothbrush](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-3.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

The body of the smart, app-connected toothbrush contains a zero-gravity mouthrinse chamber.
Credit: Dyson

![the dyson camera jet toothbrush sprays a jet of water](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-4.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

The toothbrush dispenses a jet of water within 100 milliseconds of detecting a gap between your teeth.
Credit: Dyson

At the same time, Dyson says the toothbrush uses "variable sonic oscillation" so the bristles can penetrate and clean deeper than conventional sonic toothbrushes.

The toothbrush has a zero-gravity mouthrinse container, and it comes with a charging dock and travel case. Because it doubles as an electric flosser, the Dyson CameraJet™ has a larger body than most electric toothbrushes and, based on the photos, appears approximately lightsaber-sized.

## How does AI factor into all of this?

![dyson camerajet in charging dock](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-5.fill.size_2000x1500.v1788287125.jpg)

The toothbrush comes with a charging dock and travel case.
Credit: Dyson

Beauty tech and grooming brands have been using AI in their hardware for a few years now. I first noticed this trend in my pre-Mashable days, when I was reviewing grooming products for *GQ*. All of a sudden, beard trimmers and electric shavers didn't just cut your hair — they used artificial intelligence to automatically sense hair thickness and alter the motor power to optimize your trim. Dyson introduced similar technology in its hair dryers, such as the [Supersonic Nural](https://mashable.com/tech/sept-1-dyson-supersonic-nural-deal).

If this smart technology has improved the quality of my shave and beard trimming, I haven't noticed. These "smart" beauty devices have always felt to me more like a gimmick and an excuse to raise prices by $100.

You can easily picture the scene: A conference room full of branding experts making mid-six figures, telling each other they absolutely must introduce AI into their products to stay relevant and appeal to young people.

SEE ALSO:
[I found 4 Dyson Supersonic dupes that are almost as good as the real thing](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-dyson-supersonic-dupes-2026)

Dyson also isn't the first to bring AI to the bathroom sink: [Oral-B's iO Series 10](https://mashable.com/article/oral-b-io-series-9-ai-toothbrush-review) rechargeable toothbrush already uses the technology to track where you're brushing and offer [real-time feedback](https://oralb.com/en-us/products/electric-toothbrushes/io-series-10-rechargeable-electric-toothbrush-stardust-white/) on your technique — and it will set you back $399.99.

Per Dyson, the CameraJet™ has 16 million lines of code and a visual intelligence system trained on 470,000 dental images.

And while Dyson's whole brand is basically over-engineering ordinary devices (often for the better!), introducing AI into ordinary products isn't innovation so much as trend-chasing. I'll be happy to see the backside of this smart beauty trend.

I'm never going to download an app in order to use my toothbrush, and you can't make me.

Because, of course, the Dyson Camera Jet™ has an app.

"The Dyson CameraJet™ is Wi-Fi connected at 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connected," the press release states. "Its integrated camera is a high-quality endoscope, allowing users to see what their dentist sees through the live-viewing feature in the MyDysonT™ app."

But do you really want to see what your dentist sees? Does your dentist even want to see what your dentist sees?

## Is the Dyson Camera Jet™ worth it?

![dyson camerajet toothbrush in blue and white](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-6.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788287125.png)

Credit: Dyson

I have not reviewed this device, though I'd be open to trying it and being proven wrong. We've certainly seen some [bizarre toothbrush designs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kpuU2pZaANw) in recent years, and I'll admit, I'm a poor flosser.

If, like me, you know your flossing game is weak and you don't mind spending $500 on a new squirting toothbrush, then you may come to a different conclusion than I have.

But I remain extremely skeptical of this particular Dyson invention.

**You can pre-order the Dyson Camera Jet™ for $499.99 at the Dyson online store, Amazon, and other retailers; it's available in two colors, ceramic pink and ceramic ultra blue. The smart toothbrush will be officially released on Sept. 8.**

[![dyson camera jet toothbrush in ceramic pink](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4/images-7.fill.size_171x256.v1788287125.jpg)](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-image&position=2&element_label=image&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")

[Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrush](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-title&position=2&element_label=Dyson+CameraJet+electric+toothbrush&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")

$499.99
 at Amazon

[Pre-order Here at Amazon](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FDyson-CameraJetTM-Electric-Toothbrush-Precision%2Fdp%2FB0GY1VCHYH%2F&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-button&position=2&element_label=Pre-order+Here+at+Amazon&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=03uJ4FLvU6cMMd0hHZbuBcJ&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)") [Pre-order Here at Dyson](https://cc.mashable.com/v1/otc/03bCs1jQxEftXGkZ7A6Km1e?merchant=05u1UqQ5WfhsKP7roMsCqUo&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.dyson.com%2Foral-care%2Felectric-toothbrush%2Fcamerajet%2Fceramic-pink-set&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=offer-button&position=2&element_label=Pre-order+Here+at+Dyson&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&product_uuid=07xv5zoCMAyMR4U5yid0Byt&offer_uuid=01aUi1nkI6N519XTLoLUNmD&pageview_type=RSS&object_type=article&object_uuid=03bdvurKylVMEhamXS2BWL4 "(opens in a new window)")
