entries.title: Apple’s loaded September kicks off with ‘huge launch’ next week
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

September is always the biggest month of the year for Apple fans. That’s when we get the new operating systems first announced at WWDC in June, new iPhones, new Apple Watches, and sometimes more.

This year is especially monumental. It’s the first month and the first event helmed by new CEO John Ternus, the release of the biggest OS updates in years with an all-new Siri, and the unveiling of Apple’s first folding iPhone. All that and more are coming this September. Here’s what’s on the way.

## New CEO, new iPhone, and more

As of September 1, Tim Cook is out as CEO (taking a backseat role as Chairman) and new CEO John Ternus is at the helm. That means the big Apple event on September 9 will be the first not headlined by Cook in 15 years. In his welcome letter to employees, he promised a “huge launch that’s going to be phenomenal.” With Ternus at the helm, will the Surprise and Shine event be different in tone or structure from what we’ve seen the last few years? We’ll find out on September 9 at 10 am. Here’s what we expect at the event:

**iPhone Ultra:** The marquee product of the new lineup will be Apple’s first foldable device, likely to be called iPhone Ultra. We already have a good idea of its design, but we don’t yet know about its features, particularly what Apple is doing with the software. We expect the price to top $2,000.

**iPhone 18 Pro/Max:** The [iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2953687/iphone-18-pro-2026-release-date-design-specs-rumors.html) will be an evolutionary upgrade from the iPhone 17 Pro. The big updates are a faster A20 Pro processor and a new main camera with variable aperture.

**Apple Watch Series 12:** We don’t expect much to be new about the [Apple Watch Series 12. There should be a faster processor,](https://www.macworld.com/article/3177024/apple-watch-series-12-2026-design-features-specs-release-date.html) and Apple is said to be bringing back the ceramic case option, but the rumors say not to expect a change to the design or major new features this year.

**Apple Watch Ultra 4:** Just like the Series 12, the new Ultra is going to be primarily a “chip and ship” update with no major design changes or new features.

![Surprise and Shine apple](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/surprise-and-shine-apple.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple’s iPhone event will be loaded with shiny new products—and hopefully some surprises.

Apple

**AirPods 5:** Apparently, there’s an AirPods 5 that could ship as early as September. Like AirPods 4, it would come in both standard and active noise-cancelling versions, but we’re not sure what will actually be new. This is not expected to be the AirPods with cameras in them, and it’s unknown what the new features might be.

**Apple TV 4K:** A new-generation Apple TV box with a new processor that supports the new Siri AI is supposed to ship before the end of the year. It could be announced at the September event, or it could just go up on the website one day. There’s plenty of time for this update to be released in later months, too.

**HomePod mini:** Just like the new Apple TV box, the main reason for this to exist is to get a new chip that supports Siri AI. As with the Apple TV, this may not even get mentioned at the event at all and could just go up on the website as an update anytime this year.

**Smart home hub:** The biggest question mark for Apple’s upcoming event is whether or not the company will unveil its [new home hub device](https://www.macworld.com/article/3201176/apples-big-siri-ai-powered-smart-home-hub-is-nearly-here.html). This is said to be a tablet-like pad, with a new 7-inch squarish shape, that will come in both base/speaker-mounted or wall-mounted varieties. It will run a new operating system that blends some of the features of Apple Watch and Apple TV. It’s meant to control your smart home stuff, make FaceTime calls, listen to music, and so on. Rumors say it could launch this fall, but that doesn’t necessarily mean September.

**Mac mini and Mac Studio:** While announced in August, the new [M6 / M5 Pro Mac mini](https://www.macworld.com/article/2964754/2026-mac-mini-m5-pro-design-specs-release-date.html) and [M5 Max/Ultra Mac Studio](https://www.macworld.com/article/2973459/2026-mac-studio-m5-release-date-specs-price-rumors.html) are actually shipping starting on September 22.

## Apps and software updates

![Siri AI on an iPhone 17 Pro running  iOS 27](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Siri-AI-iOS-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

A whole new Siri is coming with iOS 27.

Apple

**The OS 27 updates:** All the “27” updates are getting ready for release in September. This is a huge release, with a complete overhaul for Siri, turning it into a real AI chatbot agent, as well as dozens of quality-of-life and performance improvements. There are helpful new features throughout, many of them AI-powered, like the Phone app surfacing relevant info when calling a person or business. Call the airline and get your ticket confirmation number from your email right on the Phone screen, for example. There are new Photos editing features, a totally new Image Playground, the ability to essentially vibe-code Shortcuts or Safari extensions, and over [250 other pain points and wishlist items](https://www.macworld.com/article/3159978/marvel-at-over-250-fixes-and-improvements-coming-in-the-apple-updates-this-fall.html) addressed.

**Siri AI:** Part of the new OS 27 updates is a new Siri, appropriately called Siri AI. It’s an entirely new generation of AI assistant, and no longer years behind other contemporary AI chatbots like Gemini, Claude, or ChatGPT. It’s more conversational and has much better world knowledge, more easily understands you and your context, and can even look through your Messages, Mail, Calendar, and Contacts to piece together personalized responses. It all comes together in a new Siri app that keeps a history of your questions and chats (you can adjust for how long the history remains) and is synced between devices.

## Services

### Apple TV+

Here are the shows, series, and movies we expect to release on Apple TV+ in TK. If you want to know what’s coming later, check our [full guide to upcoming Apple TV+ content](https://www.macworld.com/article/340717/apple-tv-plus-upcoming-shows-future-moves-series-release-dates-film-television.html).

**Mayday:** An action-packed buddy comedy film. When hotshot U.S. Navy pilot Lieutenant Troy “Assassin” Kelly (Ryan Reynolds) is sent on a top-secret mission into Russian territory at the height of the Cold War, the operation implodes, leaving him stranded behind enemy lines. **September 4**

**Last Seen:** A former police detective, now working as a dispatcher, receives a call from a teenage girl who he is convinced is his daughter, who went missing 11 years ago. **September 9**

**Slow Horses (season 6):** This darkly funny British spy thriller show is easily one of the best things on Apple TV, and it’s back for another short season. **September 16**

**Brothers:** Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrison play fictionalized versions of themselves whose lifelong friendship is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: They might actually be brothers. **September 23**

### Apple Arcade

Apple releases most Apple Arcade games on the first Friday of each month. Check our [Apple Arcade FAQ](https://www.macworld.com/article/232599/apple-arcade-faq-list-of-games-price-compatibility-coming-soon.html) for a full list of Apple Arcade games and more details on the service. Occasionally, games are released with no forewarning, but you’ll usually see next month’s releases listed in the Coming Soon section.

**Art of Fauna: Cozy Puzzles+:** Piece together over 300 pieces of animal artwork. **September 3**

**Block Blast+:** Block-based puzzles with daily puzzles and adventure mode. **September 3**

**Coloring Games for Families+:** A very family-friendly, kid-oriented coloring game. **September 3**

**Let’s Play! Oink Games+:** 9 board games from a Japanese small-box board game company. **September 3**

entries.title: Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock review: Affordable, fast – now with SSD slot option
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

![Editors' Choice](https://www.macworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/MW-EN-EC.svg)

#### At a glance

### Expert's Rating

### Pros

* 12 ports, including four Thunderbolt 5
* SSD slot option (UTD58M model)
* 2.5Gb Ethernet
* 30W USB-C at front
* 230W Power Delivery
* Affordable

### Cons

* Upstream port at front
* Four USB-A but no USB-C

### Our Verdict

As a dual-display dock with a bunch of top-rated ports the Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station is great value for money for 80Gbps speed and power, with a new model offering a speedy SSD slot.

Price When Reviewed

This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined

Best Pricing Today

### Best Prices Today: WAVLINK Thunderbolt 5 Dock (UTD58)

Retailer

Price

![amazon](https://www.macworld.com/wp-content/themes/idg-b2b-base-theme/dist/static/img/amazon-logo.svg)

[Check](https://www.amazon./s?k=WAVLINK+Thunderbolt+5+Dock+%28UTD58%29)

Price comparison from over 24,000 stores worldwide

**What is it?** A Thunderbolt 5 MacBook docking station with 12 fast ports plus an option for an SSD slot for extra affordable storage.

**Who is it for?**Users who require the fastest connections and those looking to add speedy storage to their MacBook setup at prices way below Apple’s own.

**Who shouldn’t buy it?** People who don’t need fast Thunderbolt connections or require more than two external displays.

The Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station is a full docking station with 12 ports, including a full four 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5 and 2.5Gb Ethernet, available at an affordable price. It features a decent rack of high-end ports, and looks fancy, too.

There are two versions: the UTD58M ([$349](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H79KTFZ6?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com)) with an integrated fast SSD slot, and the base UTD58 without ([$299](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FRG475YC?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com)).

Even if your laptop has Thunderbolt 4 (TB4) rather than Thunderbolt 5 (TB5) connectivity, buying the newer faster standard will future proof your purchase. Backwards compatible with Thunderbolt 3 and 4, TB5 features the fastest 80Gbps bandwidth (up to 120Gbps Bandwidth Boost for unidirectional video) plus smart device daisy-chaining and super-fast storage connectivity.

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station ports front and rear](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Dock-Ports-diagram.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

## Specs and features: The ports and power you get

* **One upstream Thunderbolt 5 port** (80Gbps, 140W)
* **Two downstream Thunderbolt 5 ports** (80Gbps, 15W)
* **One downstream Thunderbolt 5 port** (80Gbps, 30W)
* **Four USB-A ports** (10Gbps)
* **Ethernet** (2.5Gb)
* **SSD slot** (UTD58M model only)
* **UHS-II SD Card reader** (312MBps)
* **UHS-II MicroSD Card reader** (312MBps)
* **3.5mm audio jack**
* **230W power supply**

As well as its upstream Thunderbolt 5 port that connects to your laptop, there are three downstream TB5 ports that connect to other devices such as monitors or storage drives: one is at the front with the upstream TB5 port, and two are at the back.

Only the UTD58M model features the built-in SSD slot.

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station TB5 ports](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Docking-Station-TB5-ports.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Simon Jary

Wavlink’s Thunderbolt 4 dock had just one downstream TB4 port as it sacrificed two possible Thunderbolt ports for dedicated HDMI 2.1 ports. With this new model, Wavlink ditches the video ports to give you the choice of which TB ports to use to connect to monitors either via a direct USB-C connection or using USB-C to DisplayPort or USB-C to HDMI adapter cables.

This gives you flexibility, and if connecting two screens we expect you’ll choose the two TB5 ports at the back.

The downstream TB5 port at the front can output at 30W, which is easily enough to fast charge an iPhone or iPad. The two TB5 ports at the back can handle 15W each.

The upstream TB5 port can output at 140W (PD 3.1), which is what you need to fast-charge the 16-inch MacBook Pro so is good for the whole range.

The external power supply can provide up to 230W of power, which is a welcome boost from the company’s rather puny 160W TB4 dock.

**USB**: Thunderbolt is backwards compatible with USB-C, which uses the same end connector, so any of the TB ports not being used to connect a monitor can be used for USB-C devices as well as speedy Thunderbolt. There are four speedy 10Gbps USB-A ports. USB-A has a place for legacy devices, but do we need four of them at the expense of a spare USB-C or two?

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 dock station with SSD open](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-dock-station-with-SSD-open-2.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Simon Jary

## What are this dock’s storage options?

Both versions of the Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station feature fast storage card readers, but only the UTD58M model comes with the built-in SSD slot hidden under its base.

This slot supports high-performance PCIe Gen 4 x4 M.2 SSD with a data transfer rate of up to 64Gbps, which should significantly improve read and write speeds with no need for a port-hogging external hard drive enclosure. Data sloggers and pro studios will enjoy the local high-speed caching.

At the time of writing you could buy a 1TB NVMe SSD for [under $200](https://www.amazon.com/SANDISK-1TB-Optimus-5100-NVMe/dp/B0GJS98B1Q?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com), and [under $400](https://www.amazon.com/Samsung-SSD-990-PCIe-2280/dp/B0BHJJ9Y77?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) for 2TB. 4TB SSDs will set you back more like [$700](https://www.amazon.com/WD_BLACK-SN8100-Internal-Solid-State/dp/B0F3B6MZM9?th=1&tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com), but it’s still cheaper than Apple charges at the point of purchase and gives you a lot more flexibility.

Installing your own NVMe SSD (the dock doesn’t come with one pre-installed) is simple, using the included screwdriver as shown above.

This isn’t the only Thunderbolt 5 dock with an integrated SSD slot—check out the [Kensington EQ Pro Thunderbolt 5 Dock for MacBook](https://www.macworld.com/article/3094898/kensington-eq-pro-thunderbolt-5-dock-for-macbook-review-sd7100ts.html), [Ugreen Maxidok 17-in-1 dock](https://www.macworld.com/article/3097185/ugreen-maxidok-17-in-1-thunderbolt-5-docking-station-review-plenty-of-ports-plus-ssd-slot-storage-flexibility.html), and [Sonnet Echo 21 SuperDock](https://www.macworld.com/article/3145505/sonnet-echo-21-thunderbolt-5-superdock-review.html)—but it is the most affordable of those we have tested.

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station SD](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Docking-Station-SD.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Simon Jary

**Card readers**: Although Apple’s MacBook Pro laptop includes a 250MBps card reader, having one on the dock is convenient. The Wavlink TB5 dock has two: one SD and one MicroSD, both at the fastest 312MBps. These are nicely placed at the front for easy access.

Such cards offer very affordable and extremely portable storage. At the time of writing you could get a 512GB SD card for under $50, although faster cards are pricier.

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station Ethernet](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Docking-Station-Ethernet.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Simon Jary

**Ethernet:** While WiFi is great for phone use, sometimes hooking up to the home or office wired network gives you faster and more stable downloads. Most local area networks (LANs) use 1Gb Ethernet, known as Gigabit Ethernet or 1GbE. Increasingly networks are moving to much faster 2.5GbE, 5GbE or even 10GbE. The Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock offers 2.5GbE, which is backwards compatible with 1GbE so even if you’re not yet on the faster network speed you’ll be ready for it when you do.

**Other ports**: At the front there’s an anti-theft Kensington Security Slot (also called a K-Slot) and a combo 3.5mm In/Out audio jack.

## Wavlink dock’s display capabilities

For most people the number one reason for buying a docking station is to easily add external screens to their laptop. Connect a cable from the dock to each monitor and you massively extend your screen real estate.

While the dock can support up to three displays for Windows laptops, limitations in Apple’s setup limit you to just two, unless you install third-party software such as DisplayLink that can give you access to up to five external displays. Five!

However, for three or more monitors the dock needs to support DisplayLink, and the Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock isn’t one of those. See our reviews of the [best DisplayLink docks](https://www.macworld.com/article/675869/how-to-connect-two-or-more-external-displays-to-apple-silicon-m1-macs.html#best-multiscreen-hubs-and-adapters-for-m1-m2-and-m3-macbooks) for options, but note that at the time of writing there were no Thunderbolt 5 DisplayLink docks. Your only solution for TB5 plus three displays without DisplayLink is the [iVanky FusionDock Max 2](https://www.macworld.com/article/2979599/ivanky-fusiondock-max-2-review-thunderbolt-5-dock.html), which has a nifty dual-chip arrangement that uses two of the MacBook’s Thunderbolt ports.

The Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock supports up to two 6K at 60Hz displays for most M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max/ MacBooks or any M4/M5 models.

These MacBooks could opt for a single 8K/60Hz display instead.

Non-Pro/Max M1/M2/M3 MacBooks support single 4K or 6K monitors. DisplayLink is also useful if your MacBook is running one of those plain M1 or M2 processors as Apple further limits those laptops to a single display. That’s by the by as M1 MacBook owners are unlikely to be in the market for a Thunderbolt 5 dock, and it’s time we got back to the review.

![Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station MacBook](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Docking-Station-MacBook.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Simon Jary

## Futuristic design looks great on any desk

The Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock is a smart aluminum build with some futuristic cooling vents at the top. Underneath are silicone pads that raise the dock off the desk surface for stability and further cooling. On the UTD58M the base is where you’ll find the SSD slot secured with a single screw.

I’m not a fan of having the upstream Thunderbolt port at the front of the dock as it’s the one cable you know will always be in use, so we prefer it hidden around the back. Ideally, given the choice I’d have all the Thunderbolt ports at the back and a spare USB-C port at the front for charging. But that’s not how Wavlink has laid out its ports. Still, having three downstream ports is more than some docking stations offer and we’re happy with that.

Wavlink has included an on/off button, which is appreciated. Although Apple has made the MacBook clever enough to manage its power in a sensible fashion, I still like to turn off power to the laptop’s battery as I don’t want it constantly kept filled to 100% when I’m not using it. A power button means I don’t have to yank the cable out to break the power between the dock and the laptop when I’ve finished working.

####

### WAVLINK Thunderbolt 5 Dock (UTD58)

![WAVLINK Thunderbolt 5 Dock (UTD58)](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-Docking-Station-front-5.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

![Editors' Choice](https://www.macworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/MW-EN-EC.svg)

[Read our review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3009184/wavlink-thunderbolt-5-dock-review.html)

####

### WAVLINK Thunderbolt 5 Dock with SSD Slot (UTD58M)

![WAVLINK Thunderbolt 5 Dock with SSD Slot (UTD58M)](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Wavlink-Thunderbolt-5-dock-station-with-SSD-open-2.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

## How much do the Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 docks cost?

At [$299.99](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FRG475YC?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) or [£239.99](https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0FRG475YC?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com), the base-level Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Dock is priced below most Thunderbolt 5 docks. It shares the sub-$300 price point with the [Plugable Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station](https://www.macworld.com/article/2856593/plugable-thunderbolt-5-docking-station-tbt-udt3-review.html), and has a similar array of ports, although it has one more and faster USB-A ports. The Wavlink also wins on a higher overall power supply: 230W vs 180W.

The Plugable can stand either vertically or lie flat like the Wavlink and sensibly places the upstream TB5 port at the back. The Wavlink’s 30W front TB5 port beats the Plugable’s 15W front TB5 port. Otherwise, they are very similar in terms of tech specs.

The [$349](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H79KTFZ6?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) / [£349](https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0H79KTFZ6?tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) UTD58M model with SSD slot will set you back another $50 plus the cost of whichever capacity and speed NVMe SSD that you can afford. Pay the extra $50 for the UTD58M if you want fast, inexpensive desktop storage built into the dock; otherwise the standard UTD58 offers essentially the same docking features for less.

See our roundups of the [best Thunderbolt docks for Mac](https://www.macworld.com/article/668894/best-thunderbolt-3-4-and-usb-c-docking-stations-for-macbook-pro-and-air.html?i) for other comparable solutions.

## Which Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station should you buy?

While its triple-monitor potential is muted on Macs—Apple’s limitation, not the dock’s—as a dual-display dock with a bunch of top-rated ports the Wavlink Thunderbolt 5 Docking Station and an SSD slot option is great value for money for 80Gbps speed and power. The new model with SSD slot offers high-speed data transfer and lower latency for demanding jobs with greater flexibility than you get from Apple when you purchase your Mac.

entries.title: Sonic the Hedgehog trading cards are coming — everything that collectors need to know
entries.content:
![Sonic the Hedgehog trading cards](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/hero-image.jpg)

**TL;DR:** [Panini](https://zdcs.link/9YJJV2?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Panini&object_type=article&object_uuid=02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs&short_url=9YJJV2&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") is launching its first Sonic the Hedgehog trading card collection, featuring classic and modern versions of Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, Amy, and Dr. Eggman, plus rare Color Blast, Kaboom!, Tie-Dye Prizms, and 1-of-1 Black Prizms.

---

Sonic the Hedgehog is getting the [trading card](https://mashable.com/category/trading-cards) treatment for the first time, thanks to [Panini America](https://zdcs.link/9YJJV2?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Panini%20America&object_type=article&object_uuid=02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs&short_url=9YJJV2&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)"). The new collection brings together characters from across the franchise's classic and modern eras, with a mix of standard cards and harder-to-find inserts.

![Knuckles Sonic the Hedgehog](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/images-2.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

Credit: Sonic the Hedgehog

![Sonic the Hedgehog](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/images-3.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

Credit: Sonic the Hedgehog

And if you're into the whole thrill-of-the-pull side of collecting, there are some rare cards hiding in these packs. Sonic is obviously front and center, but Tails, Knuckles, Amy, and Dr. Eggman are all also along for the ride.

There are also several themed inserts to look for, including Negative Space, Eggman Empire, and Artistry in Motion. So there's more to chase than just the main character cards.

![Negative Space](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/images-4.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

Credit: Sonic the Hedgehog

![Eggman Empire](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/images-5.fit_lim.size_376x.jpg)

Credit: Sonic the Hedgehog

## The cards to chase

For collectors who like hunting the big pulls, Panini is adding several ultra-rare and limited-edition cards to the mix. The collection includes Color Blast and Kaboom! cards featuring Sonic and other characters.

![Color Blast](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02HRuFdlhqTbapeTdJUipDs/images-6.fill.size_2000x1429.v1788290450.jpg)

Credit: Sonic the Hedgehog

There are also Tie-Dye Prizms numbered to five, meaning only five copies of each specific card exist, along with 1-of-1 Black Prizms that are, as the name suggests, one-of-a-kind.

## How to collect

Panini is releasing the Sonic collection in Hobby, Hobby Preferred, and retail configurations, so collectors will have different ways to get into the set. The Hobby configuration comes with six cards per pack, six packs per box, and 12 boxes per case.

The collection spans Sonic's classic and modern eras, so whether you've been following the Blue Blur since Green Hill Zone or came to the franchise more recently, there's plenty of familiar stuff to hunt down.

Now, all that’s left is to see which Sonic card you will pull first.

entries.title: Churchill Downs urges FTC review of HISA as regulator suspends trainer over alleged Albuterol violations
entries.content:
![HISA Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority logo amid FTC scrutiny over governance, data security and horse racing enforcement. Churchill Downs urges FTC review of HISA as regulator suspends trainer over alleged Albuterol violations](https://readwrite.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Churchill-Downs-urges-FTC-review-of-HISA-as-regulator-suspends-trainer-over-alleged-Albuterol-violations-300x200.png)

[Churchill Downs Incorporated](https://readwrite.com/kentucky-derby-breaks-records-with-349m-wagering-handle/) has asked the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to order an independent review of the Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority, escalating scrutiny of the regulator days before HISA provisionally suspended trainer Angel Quiroz over a series of alleged medication and horse-welfare violations.

In an [August 28 letter](https://production-picks-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/2026/08/FTC-Letter-08.28.26.pdf) to FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson and Commissioner Mark Meador, Churchill Downs said a series of recent events had raised “significant questions about the governance, transparency, technology controls, and accountability” of HISA. The company asked the FTC, which oversees HISA, to require or initiate a formal independent review covering racing and wagering integrity, non-public information and the safeguarding of sensitive industry data.

The intervention follows controversy over the so-called “Fair Hill Five” betting episode and HISA’s handling of confidential veterinary information accessed through its online portal by horse racing data analyst and owner Marshall Gramm.

The [latest enforcement action came on August 31](https://ruling-document-prod-new.s3.amazonaws.com/R001744786/RulingFormType.ruling/a11cc6f2-51da-4278-8215-f41113db34c0.pdf?AWSAccessKeyId=ASIAZPPGAALTXL5SSQGB&Signature=tSsc%2FrDoU7nzpMrFFjbw%2BfGcwWU%3D&x-amz-security-token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEPr%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJIMEYCIQDGqRVXQA%2Fi%2Fzlb6cAx5%2BABxUwmwEyvwEddJUhC7G0jagIhAL8UZHZizb1csCc0OzULi8QK7qAKgyWl5FqNL6wqhDfMKocECMP%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEQABoMNjUxNzA2NzYxOTU5IgyWMwCQ6ty6XUEXqhoq2wN8racIjfoZpG1HFpVpIAXEmOp5Yw7FgPJUq%2FL04AWO%2B8EZw%2FVzLxmHx0s7ZzJhMgHLsGWDzlp9z3Xhr94bi8FC%2B%2F9Jc5voz1%2BSZB4tTySyl71y119u%2BNxaPQ2eEsk08dJlz8zVutghwLkeC338SPPdsqy3F0muJgaoYPqOBXVwjxXFc2H1I7wZV%2FyleU%2B%2BPDgRS07tv5tAxxUTIuGsGakwqrYuYWCfUWatY8d8FvsXdrHGZQYwiEVcJ0Ba8Aec2DCMdeki3NxbHWjcf11UUCuDFCna2B%2F2EWjpeX1RLgvBfFbL%2FaTw8hGxTzAgsZS2%2BoALCf%2F4sWlTbqFqbjLwC8AzKERrNRLWPNcJWhCSDItnMbjQ8E%2FyZJK14HbGA6M9zjNyb6ykWvYBqqj1Usq%2Fq4wa8rvj6ArVSyJ2OeB8hSoKsvBv7BHQWo8nGRvlKgQZLWf7W5d4wF5A%2FBuG%2FkjlXAovV04wyZfP8M5cm5mvFLFWKHkZaVBwPI8Dn%2BLzljdK%2F%2BMvjVLLfqH8PoHQrA9fFTbC6ZTo%2B%2FqEdKS50AejssANqwaIUI5pWrtvDiFgRtnHtcSp9Bnsu2GVTs2horBk7YuZ8PUKPSBIubJefB4tdE7uV77CvqYT1fu2oQwXMKbl39QGOqABlQRYZGnSBYQJnOmHP7sw7rQwM%2F4GxRW8kHFbGnkQ0D4wmmLx1g7E4sp6vN2sBjngkVbVGEAwiSCNgxOm1uki9gpJ2L%2F0qeMBVyGOSgWV7cvVurE0I05qzSj176%2ByoTrX16o8jRlDTxYrLnAveHQ6dAEL2ndMA51VVBXtjkLYOUHpQE7XnZW3TEMOjez0YGlV%2FJ4yY%2FU54LYAGeZmfr3QnQ%3D%3D&Expires=1788947977), when HISA served Quiroz with a notice alleging violations of Rules 2215 and 2221. His registration was provisionally suspended from noon EDT on September 1, pending a provisional hearing. The notice says HISA believed there was “clear and convincing evidence” that his actions or inactions presented an immediate threat of serious injury or death to covered horses or riders.

HISA alleges three horses under Quiroz’s care, Bonita Rough, Scootaloo and Tepeyac, returned adverse analytical findings for Albuterol, which is classified as a banned substance unless prescribed in specified circumstances. Each alleged anti-doping violation involving a banned substance carries a potential two-year period of ineligibility and $25,000 fine.

## Quiroz suspended after three horses test positive for Albuterol

The first case involved Bonita Rough, whose blood sample was collected after a Vet’s List Workout at Fair Hill Training Center in Maryland on July 10.

According to the notice, laboratory analysis detected Albuterol, while HISA Portal records showed no dispensation, prescription or treatment with the drug during the period Quiroz was the horse’s Responsible Person.

HISA’s filing says Quiroz subsequently told investigators he had nebulised Bonita Rough with Albuterol obtained from the horse’s veterinarian at Gulfstream.

“You stated that you nebulized Bonita Rough with Albuterol that you received from Bonita Rough’s Veterinarian at Gulfstream,” the charge letter quoted in the notice says. “You stated the Veterinarian had prescribed the medication to another horse but informed you that you could use it on Bonita Rough if needed.”

HISA alleges that this amounted to administering a controlled medication outside a valid veterinarian-client-patient relationship. Its notice also says no corresponding Albuterol treatment records existed in the HISA Portal for Bonita Rough, Scootaloo or Tepeyac.

The regulator said Quiroz was notified of the potential Bonita Rough violation on July 28. Thirteen days later, an out-of-competition sample was collected from Scootaloo at Saratoga Race Course and subsequently tested positive for Albuterol, according to the notice.

A sample taken from Tepeyac at Fair Hill on August 13, 16 days after the initial notification concerning Bonita Rough, also returned an adverse analytical finding for Albuterol, HISA said.

HISA said the alleged discovery of banned substances in multiple horses after Quiroz had already been notified of the first case posed an “immediate threat of serious injury or death to Covered Horses or Riders”. The allegations remain subject to the disciplinary process.

Quiroz also faces a separate allegation that he caused Bonita Rough to breach her provisional suspension by posting a timed and reported workout at Fair Hill on July 29.

## Churchill Downs says HISA scrutiny goes beyond Gramm

The Quiroz action comes as Churchill Downs is challenging HISA over broader questions about its technology, oversight and disclosure practices.

Its August 28 FTC letter focused heavily on the controversy surrounding Gramm’s access to confidential veterinary and horse-health information through the HISA Portal.

HISA announced on August 17 that it had [charged Gramm with multiple rule violations](https://bphisaweb.wpengine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Press-Release-HISA-Charges-Marshall-Gramm-with-Multiple-Rule-Violations-Including-Fraud-Over-Unauthorized-Access-to-Confidential-Horse-Health-Information.pdf), including fraud, after an investigation into confidential information appearing in past-performance reports for Deterministic and Griffin’s Wharf. HISA said the information should only have been available to the horses’ connections and regulatory veterinarians.

> Following a comprehensive review that involved internal and third-party expert investigators, HISA has levied charges against Marshall Gramm for multiple violations of HISA rules arising from unauthorized access of confidential horse health information.<https://t.co/1K2WUjd8IH> [pic.twitter.com/NFNzwSOw6r](https://t.co/NFNzwSOw6r)
>
> — Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority (@hisa\_us) [August 17, 2026](https://x.com/hisa_us/status/2089400655202996255?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

HISA said its investigation, which included an independent forensic cybersecurity analysis, concluded Gramm had deliberately accessed confidential information over approximately six weeks and developed an automated method for obtaining it “at scale” in a way designed to mimic authorized activity and avoid detection.

Gramm has disputed HISA’s characterisation of his conduct. In a public statement, he said the information was available through his authorised HISA account and that he used his own credentials, did not conceal his identity and bypassed no security protocols or safeguards.

> My statement on HISA Matter  
> HISA has unfortunately decided to pursue disciplinary proceedings against me regarding data I accessed through the HISA Portal. I made a good-faith effort to resolve this matter with HISA, and we came very close to doing so.  
>   
> Ultimately, we could not…
>
> — Marshall Gramm (@marshallgramm) [August 17, 2026](https://x.com/marshallgramm/status/2089407419004711254?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

“I intend to vigorously defend myself in the HISA proceedings,” Gramm said.

He acknowledged exercising “poor judgment” by failing to alert HISA sooner to the vulnerability after the issue became public, but argued that focusing on him distracted from weaknesses in HISA’s systems.

The Jockey Club separately said Gramm had accessed veterinary information relating to horses he did not own and announced that its stewards would meet to take steps to remove him as a member.

> Statement from The Jockey Club: Marshall Gramm / HISA  
>   
> Based upon an investigation by HISA, Marshall Gramm, a Thoroughbred breeder, owner, and a member of The Jockey Club, accessed veterinary information for horses he did not own within a system operated by HISA. His membership…
>
> — The Jockey Club (@jockeyclub) [August 18, 2026](https://x.com/jockeyclub/status/2089723753085227467?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

## Portal controversy raises questions over HISA security controls

Churchill Downs told the FTC it was not seeking to “excuse, minimize, or prejudge” any alleged misconduct by Gramm. Instead, it argued that the controversy exposed a separate institutional problem.

“But the institutional question is separate and more fundamental: why was such information accessible in the first place?” the company said.

The company stressed what it characterized as a reversal in HISA’s public explanation of the episode. According to the letter, HISA CEO Lisa Lazarus had initially said screenshots circulating online could not have originated from the HISA Portal, before HISA later acknowledged the health information had come from its system.

Churchill Downs said HISA’s subsequent focus on allegations of “fraud”, “misappropriation” and other wrongdoing by Gramm did not answer critical questions about the regulator’s own controls.

Among them were how an authorised user could access records for horses with which they had no legitimate connection, whether similar vulnerabilities existed elsewhere, whether other users accessed comparable information, how long the vulnerability existed and why it was not detected sooner.

HISA, meanwhile, said it had changed its technology systems to prevent similar unauthorised access and was devoting additional resources to protecting confidential information.

“There must be significant consequences for individuals who violate the integrity of our rules and obtain and abuse confidential horse health information,” Lazarus said. “HISA will take every necessary step to fiercely protect the integrity of Thoroughbred racing and ensure that violators of our rules are punished appropriately.”

## Churchill Downs seeks independent review of HISA governance

Churchill Downs wants the FTC review to extend well beyond the Gramm case.

Its letter calls for an independent examination of the Fair Hill Five episode, the timing and disclosure of a previously undisclosed banned-substance positive connected with the matter, the HISA Portal vulnerability, whether other users downloaded or shared confidential information, and HISA’s relationships with technology providers.

The company also questioned whether HISA’s procurement, vendor oversight and information-security governance were appropriate for an organisation exercising federally authorised regulatory powers.

“HISA’s legitimacy depends on confidence that it is transparent, accountable, technologically competent, and subject to meaningful oversight,” Churchill Downs said.

It added that restoring confidence would require more than assurances that individual wrongdoers would be punished.

“It will require an independent accounting of what happened, why it happened, whether it could happen again, and whether HISA’s governance and technology infrastructure are adequate for the responsibilities it has been given,” the company said.

HISA’s own materials state that it operates under FTC oversight and that its national racing integrity framework is subject to federal review.

*Featured image: HISA via [press release](https://hisaus.org/news/hisa-charges-marshall-gramm-with-multiple-rule-violations-including-fraud-over-unauthorized-access-to-confidential-horse-health-information)*

The post [Churchill Downs urges FTC review of HISA as regulator suspends trainer over alleged Albuterol violations](https://readwrite.com/churchill-downs-urges-ftc-review-hisa-quiroz-marshall-gramm/) appeared first on [ReadWrite](https://readwrite.com).

entries.title: Iran-linked APT Mirage Kitten Uses Fake Job Tests to Spread Malware
entries.content:
## **Mirage Kitten used fake LinkedIn coding tests to spread NodeRabbit and PollCat, even banning AI tools that could have spotted the malware.**

Iran-linked Mirage Kitten hackers just found a genuinely clever way to make their own malware harder to detect: telling job candidates not to use AI tools while reviewing the trojanized code they were sent. Kaspersky’s research documented two previously undocumented malware families from the APT group, delivered through fake coding challenges sent to job seekers on LinkedIn.

The setup is almost embarrassingly simple once you see it laid out. A fake recruiter contacts a software engineer, offers a role, and sends a coding assessment hosted on a completely legitimate-looking Amazon S3 link, the kind of hosting nobody would think twice about.

*“During recent threat research, we detected suspicious activity on a system in Afghanistan. We traced it to an archive containing a software development project that the user may have received during a job application process.” reads the [report](https://securelist.com/mirage-kitten-new-backdoors-noderabbit-pollcat/121244/) published by Kaspersky. “The archive purported to contain a coding challenge for candidates applying for an engineering role.”*

The archive includes a README with a three-hour time limit and an explicit rule against using AI assistants, which sounds like a normal anti-cheating measure until you realize what it’s actually preventing.

Kaspersky spells out exactly why that rule exists.

*“The README also imposed a three-hour time limit and prohibited the use of AI assistants.”states the report. “Notably, an AI code-review assistant tasked with auditing the project would likely have flagged the suspicious first-line import of an unknown npm package and warned the targeted developer that the project was trojanized.”*

the researchers write, which means the “no AI” instruction isn’t about fairness in a coding test at all, it’s a deliberate move to stop the one tool most likely to catch the malware before it runs.

The first malware family, called NodeRabbit, is written entirely in Node.js and can run on Windows, Linux, and macOS from the same codebase. That’s a change for Mirage Kitten, which has traditionally used malware written in C, C++ and Go.

NodeRabbit is hidden inside a fake npm package included in the coding test rather than published online. Once the victim runs it, the malware starts a background process and connects to infrastructure hosted on Azure, using AES-256-GCM encryption to protect its communications.

Newer versions added checks to detect sandboxes and analysis environments. The malware looks at system memory, the number of CPU cores and how long the machine has been running before deciding whether to continue.

One sample found in Egypt takes that trick a step further. When NodeRabbit suspects it’s being analyzed, it first sends a few harmless requests to Google, Microsoft and Cloudflare, then stops without contacting its real command server. That helps its traffic look like normal background activity instead of an obvious connection to the attackers.

A third variant, found on a system in Ethiopia, expanded the malware’s command set from 11 to 23 and added something genuinely unusual: the ability to plant a fake VS Code extension disguised as “GitHub Copilot Helper,” complete with a stolen publisher name to look legitimate, plus a technique that quietly injects a malicious launcher into a Git repository’s hooks so the malware relaunches every time someone merges or checks out code.

The second malware family, PollCat, takes a stranger route to establish itself. It’s disguised as a React coding challenge that requires entering a six-digit access code supposedly provided by the recruiter, with a ticking countdown designed to pressure the victim into working fast without scrutinizing anything.

*“While tracking NodeRabbit infections, we discovered another malicious tool we dubbed PollCat, which is also distributed under the guise of a programming challenge. The sample we obtained resides inside `RankChallenge-react`, a React code-fixing challenge presented as a time-limited developer assessment. Running the project invokes `npm i && node index.js`, which starts the local application and attempts to open the challenge in the user’s browser.” states the report. “*

[![](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-4.png?resize=1024%2C320&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-4.png?ssl=1)

What victims don’t realize is that PollCat starts running and begins talking to its command server the moment the application loads, well before anyone types in that access code at all.

Kaspersky linked both malware families to Mirage Kitten with high confidence. Researchers compared PollCat’s network code with an older backdoor called Retrograde, also known as MiniFast, and found that the two use almost the same connection process.

One detail is especially telling: both malware families treat an HTTP 400 error as a successful registration and extract a session token from the response. That unusual behavior is unlikely to appear by chance in two unrelated malware families.

Victims identified so far cluster in fintech and aviation organizations across Egypt, Ethiopia, and Afghanistan, consistent with Mirage Kitten’s long-standing focus on the Middle East and Africa. If your organization does any hiring through LinkedIn outreach involving take-home coding assessments, this is worth flagging to your engineering team directly, because the lure here isn’t a suspicious email with bad grammar, it’s a completely normal-looking job opportunity with a legitimate cloud-hosted download link and a plausible-sounding reason not to use the one tool that would have caught it.

*“Mirage Kitten’s latest activity marks a notable evolution in the group’s tooling: NodeRabbit and PollCat are the group’s first Node.js/JavaScript-based implants, departing from its usual native malware deployed through DLL search-order hijacking.” concludes the report.*

*“The delivery mechanism, however, remains consistent with Mirage Kitten’s historical tradecraft: the use of recruiter personas on LinkedIn to target critical sectors across the Middle East and Africa for cyberespionage purposes. We continue to track the group’s activity and will report on new developments in future publications.”*

**Follow me on Twitter:**[**@securityaffairs**](https://twitter.com/securityaffairs)**and**[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/sec.affairs)**and**[**Mastodon**](https://infosec.exchange/@securityaffairs)

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

**(**[**SecurityAffairs**](http://securityaffairs.co/wordpress/)**– hacking, Mirage Kitten)**

entries.title: Sonos Has New Devices, a New OS, and Yes, a New App
entries.content:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Wired: Sonos has a new app. Stop me if you've heard this one before. The smart speaker company, long a darling of the audio industry, undid much of the goodwill it earned with its multiroom speakers through a bevy of software updates that broke its app in 2024. Almost all app users hated it, citing the loss of features like volume control and accessibility tools meant to help blind people use the wireless speaker system. Sonos eventually owned up to the mistake, considered bringing back the old app again, then booted its CEO and marched its new leaders out to apologize profusely to win back the company's furious customers.
Now, Sonos says it has a brand-new app update, infused with lots of generative AI features. The company also announced a new soundbar and its second pair of over-the-ear headphones. Sonos representatives say it doesn't want to be seen as a speaker company anymore, but as something bigger and more holistic. "For years people have been seeing us as a speaker company," says Brandon Holley, the interim hardware lead at Sonos. "What we actually are is an audio operating system." The company is calling that operating system Sonos 27, and it manifests in a few ways.
[...] This is a lot of change for Sonos, something the company hasn't always handled gracefully. Sonos' home systems already aren't the easiest to set up, sometimes requiring separate apps for older products. The company may be rejiggering itself as an "audio operating system," but its software has long been the source of its troubles with getting its products to work right. Will AI smarts fix that? Maybe for its newer devices. But anyone with an existing system may still struggle. The AI features on products and in the Sonos 27 app will be opt-in, meaning you can avoid them entirely. "That really is our new approach to our app release," Patel says. "We're going to bring our customers along. We're going to listen more." That would be a good plan. Sounds like Sonos' speakers will be listening more, too. Sonos is emphasizing a more "customer-centric feedback listening approach" after the backlash to its previous redesign. Improvements include easier tab navigation, better room sorting, revamped volume controls, and new system-health tools for diagnosing connection problems.
The centerpiece is Sonos 27voice, a generative AI voice assistant that can handle conversational music requests, connect with services like ChatGPT through Model Context Protocol, and power customizable "Sonos Custom Agents" for tasks such as automatically activating certain speakers. "Obviously AI is something that's very hot these days," Sonos software VP Sid Patel said. "So we have integrated various pieces of AI into our system." However, the features will only work with the newer S2 app, and Sonos cautions that "not every product will support every new feature," with detailed compatibility information coming later.
Sonos is also branding its multiroom networking technology Sonos Fabric, which what Patel calls "the magic that has existed for what Sonos was built on." New Fabric features include portable surround, which lets users temporarily move speakers between rooms and have them automatically configure themselves for surround sound, and Headphone Linking, which lets users seamlessly switch audio between Sonos speakers and headphones.

[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/twitter_icon_large.png)](http://twitter.com/home?status=Sonos+Has+New+Devices%2C+a+New+OS%2C+and+Yes%2C+a+New+App%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fentertainment.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F09%2F02%2F0543221%2F%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_medium%3Dtwitter)
[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/facebook_icon_large.png)](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fentertainment.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F09%2F02%2F0543221%2Fsonos-has-new-devices-a-new-os-and-yes-a-new-app%3Futm_source%3Dslashdot%26utm_medium%3Dfacebook)

[Read more of this story](https://entertainment.slashdot.org/story/26/09/02/0543221/sonos-has-new-devices-a-new-os-and-yes-a-new-app?utm_source=rss1.0moreanon&utm_medium=feed) at Slashdot.
